snip.t: Clinical distinction: In adults, colorectal carcinoma is an important cause of large bowel obstruction.
The likely diagnosis is large-bowel obstruction secondary to colorectal carcinoma.

In parts of Africa it accounts for more than 50% of intestinal obstruction (and it is the commonest cause of large bowel obstruction in many African hospitals), unlike Western countries where cancer is the usual cause.
snip.s: Sigmoid and Caecal Volvulus: Diagnosis and Management

snip.t: Large bowel obstruction: colorectal cancer (about 60%), diverticular stricture, then volvulus (sigmoid volvulus is relatively common in Africa).
snip.s: Intestinal Obstruction in Adults: Causes, Diagnosis and Management

snip.t: ❏ Large bowel obstruction:​ ​Pseudo-obstruction is treated non-operatively.
Clinical differences between small and large bowel obstruction
In large-bowel obstruction, the colon may be dilated, with haustral markings that do not generally cross the entire bowel lumen.
Differential diagnosis: other causes of large bowel obstruction (sigmoid cancer, giant sigmoid diverticulum, pseudo-obstruction (Ogilvie)).

qs.q: A 70‑year‑old woman develops progressive constipation, abdominal distension and a palpable left lower quadrant mass. Which aetiology best explains her large bowel obstruction?
qs.e: Colorectal carcinoma is the principal cause of large bowel obstruction in adults. The other choices are either uncommon or affect different parts of the bowel.

qs.q: Which condition is a common cause of large‑bowel obstruction in the Kenyan population?
o: Fibrous scar tissue from prior surgery.
qs.e: Volvulus, especially of the sigmoid colon, is a leading aetiology of large‑bowel obstruction locally.

qs.q: A 68-year-old man presents with progressive abdominal distension, constipation, weight loss, and blood in the stool. Colonoscopy reveals a lesion causing large-bowel obstruction. What is the most common cause of large-bowel obstruction in adults?
qs.e: Colorectal carcinoma is a common cause of large-bowel obstruction where a tumour progressively narrows the lumen.

qs.q: A 67-year-old woman is admitted with a large-bowel obstruction confirmed on imaging. Under which physiological circumstance might she develop early-onset emesis mimicking proximal obstruction?
o: When peristalsis in the colon reverses direction
When the sigmoid colon is tightly twisted (volvulus)
When the ileocaecal valve fails to close properly
When a localized segment of colon becomes atonic
qs.e: While large-bowel obstruction usually presents with late vomiting, incompetence of the ileocaecal valve allows reflux of contents into the small bowel, precipitating earlier emesis. Colonic atony or twisting alone does not create this specific small-bowel reflux mechanism.

qs.q: A 60-year-old man presents with left lower quadrant colicky abdominal pain, a change in bowel habit, and clinical features of large bowel obstruction. A double-contrast barium enema is performed. Which of the following radiological findings is most characteristic of an annular left colon cancer?
o: Multiple filling defects in the caecum
qs.e: Annular napkin-ring tumours of the left colon characteristically produce an apple core appearance on a barium enema due to circumferential narrowing. Polypoid and cauliflower masses are more typical of right-sided lesions.

qs.q: A 58-year-old woman with an obstructing mid-sigmoid colon cancer presents with acute large bowel obstruction. She undergoes a one-stage resection with an end colostomy and a closed rectal stump. What is the eponym for this procedure?
qs.e: Hartmann's procedure involves resection of the obstructing sigmoid lesion with an end colostomy and a closed rectal stump. Other options in obstruction include on-table lavage or staged operations.
qs.s: Colorectal Cancer: Presentation, Staging and Surgical Management: MCQs

qs.q: A 65-year-old woman presents with absolute constipation, marked abdominal distension, and late-onset vomiting. Imaging reveals large bowel obstruction. What is the single commonest cause of large bowel obstruction?
qs.e: Colorectal cancer is the commonest cause of large bowel obstruction, accounting for about 60% of cases. Diverticular strictures and sigmoid volvulus are other causes in the large bowel.
qs.s: Intestinal Obstruction in Adults: Causes, Diagnosis and Management: MCQs

qs.q: A 70-year-old man presents with features of large bowel obstruction. A plain abdominal radiograph shows a 'coffee bean' or inverted U sign in the lower abdomen. What is the specific radiological diagnosis?
qs.e: The 'coffee bean' or inverted U sign on a plain abdominal X-ray is characteristic of a sigmoid volvulus. Caecal volvulus typically shows a dilated caecum in the left upper quadrant.
